key_insight: This paper shows that LLMs can be improved with reinforcement learning even when there is no ground-truth answer available. By turning deterministic execution feedback into a usable reward signal, RiVER enables learning on tasks that are otherwise hard to train with standard RLVR.
problem_solved: Standard reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards depends on known ground-truth solutions, which limits its use on score-based tasks where the correct answer is unknown or expensive to label. This work addresses how to train LLMs in those settings using only execution-based feedback.
method: Introduces RiVER, a ranking-induced verifiable framework for training on tasks without ground-truth solutions.
Uses deterministic execution feedback as continuous-valued supervision instead of binary correct/incorrect labels.
Applies group-relative reinforcement learning to optimize model outputs based on relative quality scores.
impact: This expands RL training to a broader class of real-world problems where exact answers are unavailable but outputs can still be evaluated. For practitioners, it offers a practical path to improve LLM performance using verifiable signals without requiring full annotations.

paper_title: Reinforcement Learning without Ground-Truth Solutions can Improve LLMs
paper_authors: Yingyu Lin, Qiyue Gao, Nikki Lijing Kuang, Xunpeng Huang, Kun Zhou
